_comment_claude_voice: claude-agent runs through the calibrated Claude Code Agent route or the separately tracked OMP-native route. It never runs through opencode_dispatch.py.
_comment_excluded_voices: Voices known to fail adversarial spec review (see registry/voices.json for calibration evidence): glm-4.7-flash — degenerate-loop behavior in both inline dispatch (paragraph repetition during reasoning-budget burnout) and subagent parallel runs (enumerated fake attacks #4-75+ on a single slice). At its ~30B 'flash' size class it is local-model tier, not gateway-frontier tier. goedel-prover-v2-32b — included in an 8-voice fan-out and produced ~8K tokens of degenerate tautology loops with abstract variable lists, 852s wall, output unusable. Theorem-prover specialists pattern-match a spec as a proof GOAL and attempt Lean/Coq tactics instead of attacking it. leanstral-2603 belongs in Lean-specific verification work, not general adversarial spec review — substitute only when the spec is a Lean theorem.
_comment_dispatch_invocation: opencode_dispatch.py passes --format json to each `opencode run` call and appends --variant automatically: the per-voice `variant` field if set, else `default_variant` below. The raw event stream is preserved per (voice, slice) as <slice>.events.jsonl; the extracted assistant text (never the JSON) feeds truncation detection and aggregation, with finish_reason and token usage recorded. No script modification needed.
_comment_slices: Slice plan. Each slice is one (voice, slice) call. headers[] are the markdown header ranges the agent should read from the target spec. attack_emphasis is the per-slice attack-category hint. Replace this example with your project's actual sections.

slices.name: scope
slices.label: System identity, non-goals, external contracts
slices.attack_emphasis: Identity overreach; non-goals that should be in scope; caller-contract clauses that admit clients the doc intends to exclude.

slices.name: behaviors-core
slices.label: Worked examples — happy path, boundary, edge, explicit failures
slices.attack_emphasis: Worked-example arithmetic; edge-case completeness; explicit-failure listing completeness; happy-path implicit assumptions.

slices.name: invariants
slices.label: Structural and behavioral invariants
slices.attack_emphasis: Pointwise evaluability of state invariants; temporal-tag correctness; coverage gaps; derived-flag soundness.

_comment_context_appendix: Optional shared-context block prepended to every call. Use for type signatures, invariant labels, or cross-section glossary entries that are load-bearing but not under attack. Mark clearly as read-only / not-to-be-attacked.
context_appendix:
=== CONTEXT APPENDIX (read-only — DO NOT ATTACK; these sections are attacked in their own invocations) ===

System under review: <your system name and one-line description>.
Intent doc: version <X.Y.Z>.

=== END CONTEXT APPENDIX ===
_comment_variant: default_variant is passed as `--variant` to every voice that lacks its own `variant` field. Canonical setting is max (maximum thinking budget on every voice that supports it). A per-voice `variant` field overrides; set it to an empty string to omit the flag for that voice.
_comment_timeouts: per_call_timeout: seconds budget per (voice, slice) call. Local reasoning models on consumer hardware can take 10-25 min per slice. max_retries: per-call retry budget on truncated stubs or HTTP errors.
_comment_isolation: Z2 isolation. Agents run in an ephemeral git worktree (detached at HEAD) with a preflight secret/symlink scan that blocks dispatch on violations; see opencode_dispatch.py ISOLATION. The child environment is reduced to a small allowlist; name any provider API keys the voices need in env_passthrough (they are read from the orchestrator's environment, never from a .env in the tree). opencode_version_pin, if set, blocks dispatch when `opencode --version` differs.
_comment_omp_native: Generated from registry/voices.json. Run from OMP with the colosseum-adversarial skill's omp_fanout.py helper. A pending calibration must be reported as uncalibrated; never borrow OpenCode fitness evidence.
